summary: Cross-task integration check across all 12 Recursive Insight tasks. Shared singletons (AIProviderClient, GraphRAG) cleanly flow via DI from existing owners (incrementalCompiler.orchestrator, WorkspaceManager) — no duplicate instantiation. TabKind enum, InsightSession placeholder swap, JS function names (loadInsightView/appendInsightDelta/setInsightDeepDives/showInsightLoading/setInsightError), and JS->Swift message types (insightDeepDiveClicked/insightSaveRequested/insightBreadcrumbClicked/insightUpClicked/insightRetryRequested) all match exactly across T5 and T6. Dependency graph is acyclic and topologically valid. Two blocking inconsistencies identified: (1) T4 instructs placeholder removal from DocumentState.swift while T2 places the placeholder in a new InsightSession.swift file (T2 AC explicitly requires the new file); (2) T6 hardcodes setInsightError retryable:true, ignoring T4's per-error-class retryability logic and the lastErrorRetryable property T4 plans to expose.

naming_mismatches.issue: T6 step 7 line 73 hardcodes `bridge.setInsightError(sessionId:, message:, retryable: true, into: webView)` regardless of error class. T4 step 10 explicitly distinguishes retryable vs non-retryable per AIProviderError case (parseError->false, noAPIKey->false, httpError 4xx other->false, vs streamingError->true, httpError 429/5xx->true). T4 implementation hint at line 222 says retryability is 'stored alongside, e.g. lastErrorRetryable: Bool' which T6 would need to subscribe to. T6's hardcoded `retryable: true` will incorrectly show the Retry button in the JS error banner for non-retryable errors (e.g., bad API key, malformed LLM response), enabling user-initiated retries that will deterministically fail.
naming_mismatches.fix: Either: (a) T4 must explicitly publish `@Published var lastErrorRetryable: Bool` in its data model and AC, and T6 must subscribe to it (e.g., via combineLatest with lastError) and pass through to setInsightError; or (b) wrap lastError as a struct `InsightError { message: String; retryable: Bool }` with a single @Published property, and T6 subscribes to that. Update T4 AC + Data Models section, update T6 step 7 + AC line referencing this subscription. JS side (T5 step 10 line 51) already accepts `retryable` parameter and behaves correctly — the gap is purely Swift-side propagation.

Not strictly cross-task, but worth flagging for completeness: T7 step 1 line 40 says 'Optionally store the session reference as @Published var activeInsightSession: InsightSession?'. T7 implementation hint line 167 says 'Do NOT add @Published var activeInsightSession if it is not strictly needed — the openTabs scan is O(N) where N <= ~20 in practice'. The two passages give opposite guidance. Reader should default to the hint (do NOT add) since openTabs scan is the simpler design.
naming_mismatches.fix: Pick one: remove the 'Optionally store' clause from step 1, OR remove the 'Do NOT add' from implementation hints. Recommend removing the Optionally-store clause and keeping the openTabs-scan as the single approach.
